'''Siv Gun Elisabeth Andersson''' (born 1959) is a Swedish [[evolutionary biologist]], professor of [[molecular evolution]] at [[Uppsala University]].<ref name="icmProfile">{{cite web | url=https://www.icm.uu.se/research/siv-andersson-en |title="Researcher Profile: Siv Andersson" | access-date=2022-03-08}}</ref> She is member of both the [[Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences]] and of [[Royal Swedish Academy of Engineering Sciences|Engineering]].<ref name="kva1">{{cite web | url=https://www.kva.se/sv/om-oss/ledamoter/siv-andersson | title="KVA Medlemssida Siv Andersson" | access-date=2022-03-09|language=sv}}</ref><ref name="iva1">{{cite web | url=https://www.iva.se/en/network/medlem?id=df4d69e9-47ce-e511-80c7-00155d018517 | access-date=2022-03-09 | title="IVA Medlemssida Andersson, Siv"|language=sv}}</ref> She is also Head of basic research at the [[Knut and Alice Wallenberg Foundation]]<ref name=wasp>{{cite web | url=https://wasp-sweden.org/new-program-on-data-driven-life-science/ | title="New Program on Data-Driven Life Science" | date=26 October 2020 | access-date=2022-03-08}}</ref> and has been co-director of the Swedish national center for large-scale research [[Science for Life Laboratory]] between 2017 and 2021.<ref name="scilifelab1">{{cite web | url=https://www.scilifelab.se/news/siv-andersson-new-co-director-for-scilifelab/ | title="Siv Andersson new Co-Director for SciLifeLab" | date=18 May 2017 |access-date=2022-03-08}}</ref> Her research focuses on the evolution of [[bacteria]], mainly on intracellular parasites.

== Education and career ==
Andersson grew up in [[Horndal]], [[Dalarna]]. Her mother was home care assistant and her father was employed in the wood industry.<ref name="curiemag">{{cite web | url=https://www.tidningencurie.se/nyheter/2017/02/28/hon-blev-dna-forskare-for-att-forsta-livet/ | title="Tidningen Curie: Hon blev DNA-forskare för att förstå livet" | date=28 February 2017 | access-date=2022-03-09|language=sv}}</ref> She studied Biology at [[Uppsala University]], since the programme was the only one that had a course about [[DNA]]. She defended her PhD in molecular biology in 1990, under the supervision of [[Charles Kurland]].<ref name="phdthesis">{{cite book|author=Andersson, Siv Gun Elisabeth.|date=1990|isbn=91-554-2551-8|oclc=22568986|publisher=Uppsala University|title=Translation, antibiotics and codon evolution}}</ref> She applied for a postdoctoral stipend from [[European Molecular Biology Organization|EMBO]] to continue her research in the United States, but ended up obtaining a research position at the MRC Laboratory of Molecular Biology in [[Cambridge]].<ref name="curiemag" /> She became professor of molecular evolution in 2000, at the Uppsala University's Evolutionary Biology Center.<ref name="curiemag" /> She was elected at the [[Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences]] in 2005.<ref name="kva1" />

Andersson has been very active in developing the Swedish national center for large-scale research [[Science for Life Laboratory]], especially its [[DNA sequencing]] and [[bioinformatics]] platforms. She served as Co-director for the center between 2017 and 2021.<ref name="scilifelab1" />

During the 2020 [[COVID-19 pandemic]], she contributed, together with Lars Engstrand and with the financial support of the [[Knut and Alice Wallenberg Foundation]], to establish the first large-scale testing facility in Sweden<ref name="coviduu">{{cite web | url=https://www.uu.se/nyheter/artikel/?id=15196&typ=artikel | title="Siv Andersson: Från nyfikenhet till nytta under pandemin" | access-date=2022-03-09|language=sv}}</ref><ref name="svd1">{{cite news | url=https://www.svd.se/wallenbergs-kupp--spelet-bakom-unika-coronalabbet | title="Wallenbergs coronakupp: byggde ett labb utan lov" | newspaper=Svenska Dagbladet | date=20 May 2020 | access-date=2022-03-09|language=sv| last1=Törnwall | first1=Mikael }}</ref>

== Research ==
Andersson's research first focused around the role of codon usage in shaping bacterial genomes.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Andersson |first1=SG |last2=Kurland |first2=CG |title=Codon preferences in free-living microorganisms. |journal=Microbiological Reviews |date=June 1990 |volume=54 |issue=2 |pages=198–210 |doi=10.1128/mr.54.2.198-210.1990 |pmid=2194095|pmc=372768 }}</ref> After her postdoctoral fellowship, she contributed to sequence one of the first genome of an obligate intracellular parasite, ''[[Rickettsia prowazekii]]'', the causative agent of epidemic typhus.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Andersson |first1=SG |last2=Zomorodipour |first2=A |last3=Andersson |first3=JO |last4=Sicheritz-Pontén |first4=T |last5=Alsmark |first5=UC |last6=Podowski |first6=RM |last7=Näslund |first7=AK |last8=Eriksson |first8=AS |last9=Winkler |first9=HH |last10=Kurland |first10=CG |title=The genome sequence of Rickettsia prowazekii and the origin of mitochondria. |journal=Nature |date=12 November 1998 |volume=396 |issue=6707 |pages=133–40 |doi=10.1038/24094 |pmid=9823893|bibcode=1998Natur.396..133A |s2cid=4379381 |doi-access=free }}</ref>

In her later career, her research continued to explore bacteria and their relationships with their different hosts.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Toft |first1=C |last2=Andersson |first2=SG |title=Evolutionary microbial genomics: insights into bacterial host adaptation. |journal=Nature Reviews. Genetics |date=July 2010 |volume=11 |issue=7 |pages=465–75 |doi=10.1038/nrg2798 |pmid=20517341|s2cid=40576224 }}</ref> In particular, she is interested in the genomic consequences of long-term associations of intracellular bacteria.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Sällström |first1=B |last2=Andersson |first2=SG |title=Genome reduction in the alpha-Proteobacteria. |journal=Current Opinion in Microbiology |date=October 2005 |volume=8 |issue=5 |pages=579–85 |doi=10.1016/j.mib.2005.08.002 |pmid=16099701}}</ref> She explored the evolution of ''[[Bartonella]]'',<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Guy |first1=L |last2=Nystedt |first2=B |last3=Toft |first3=C |last4=Zaremba-Niedzwiedzka |first4=K |last5=Berglund |first5=EC |last6=Granberg |first6=F |last7=Näslund |first7=K |last8=Eriksson |first8=AS |last9=Andersson |first9=SG |title=A gene transfer agent and a dynamic repertoire of secretion systems hold the keys to the explosive radiation of the emerging pathogen Bartonella. |journal=PLOS Genetics |date=March 2013 |volume=9 |issue=3 |article-number=e1003393 |doi=10.1371/journal.pgen.1003393 |pmid=23555299|pmc=3610622 |doi-access=free }}</ref> ''[[Wolbachia]]'',<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Klasson |first1=L |last2=Westberg |first2=J |last3=Sapountzis |first3=P |last4=Näslund |first4=K |last5=Lutnaes |first5=Y |last6=Darby |first6=AC |last7=Veneti |first7=Z |last8=Chen |first8=L |last9=Braig |first9=HR |last10=Garrett |first10=R |last11=Bourtzis |first11=K |last12=Andersson |first12=SG |title=The mosaic genome structure of the Wolbachia wRi strain infecting Drosophila simulans. |journal=Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America |date=7 April 2009 |volume=106 |issue=14 |pages=5725–30 |doi=10.1073/pnas.0810753106 |pmid=19307581|pmc=2659715 |bibcode=2009PNAS..106.5725K |doi-access=free }}</ref> and [[Planctomycetota]],<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Mahajan |first1=M |last2=Yee |first2=B |last3=Hägglund |first3=E |last4=Guy |first4=L |last5=Fuerst |first5=JA |last6=Andersson |first6=SGE |title=Paralogization and New Protein Architectures in Planctomycetes Bacteria with Complex Cell Structures. |journal=Molecular Biology and Evolution |date=1 April 2020 |volume=37 |issue=4 |pages=1020–1040 |doi=10.1093/molbev/msz287 |pmid=31808939|doi-access=free }}</ref> among others.

Andersson has published over 200 peer-reviewed articles, and has an [[h-index]] of 61, as of 2022.<ref>{{cite web |title=Google Scholar: Siv Andersson |url=https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=mnjOAcoAAAAJ&hl=en&oi=sra |website=scholar.google.com |access-date=9 March 2022}}</ref>

== Notable awards and honors ==
* 2000 - Member of the [[Royal Swedish Academy of Engineering Sciences]].<ref name="iva1" /> 
* 2002 - Letterstedtska prize for very significant investigation, among others for ''"an article in Nature (1998), which reports the whole genome sequence of the intracellular parasite Rickettsia prowazekii"''.<ref name="kva2">{{cite web | url=https://www.kva.se/sv/pressrum/pressmeddelanden/letterstedska-prisen-2002 | title="Letterstedska prisen 2002" | date=4 March 2002 | access-date=2021-01-14 | publisher=KVA|language=sv}}</ref>
* 2004 - Member of [[European Molecular Biology Organization|EMBO]].<ref name="embo1">{{cite web |title=People in the EMBO Communities |url=https://people.embo.org/profile/siv-ge-andersson |website=people.embo.org |access-date=9 March 2022}}</ref>
* 2005 - Member of the [[Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences]], number 1514, in the class Biological Sciences.<ref name="kva3">{{cite web | url=http://www.kva.se/sv/Nyheter/nyheter-2008-2001/Nya-ledamoter-invalda2/ | title="Kungl. Vetenskapsakademien: Nya ledamöter invalda, pressmeddelande 2005-02-10 | access-date=2022-03-09|language=sv}}</ref>
* 2005 - [[Göran Gustafsson Prize]] in molecular biology.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.kva.se/sv/priser/goran-gustafssonprisen/pristagare | title="Laureates" | access-date=2021-01-17 | publisher=KVA|language=sv}}</ref>
* 2005 - Grant for "excellent research" from the [[Swedish Research Council]] of SEK 44 millions (together with Hans Ellegren).<ref name="forskning1">{{cite web | title=Miljonanslag för stark forskningsmiljö till Uppsala | url=https://www.forskning.se/2005/02/17/miljonanslag-for-stark-forskningsmiljo-till-uppsala/ | date=2005-02-17 | access-date=2021-01-14|language=sv}}</ref>
* 2009 - President of the [[European Society for Evolutionary Biology]] (2009-2011).<ref>{{cite web |title=ESEB Officers - ESEB {{!}} European Society for Evolutionary Biology |url=https://eseb.org/society/officers/ |website=eseb.org}}</ref>
* 2011 - [[Knut and Alice Wallenberg Foundation|Wallenberg Scholar]].<ref name="kaw3">{{cite web |title=Bee bacteria working as vitamin factories {{!}} Knut and Alice Wallenberg Foundation |url=https://kaw.wallenberg.org/en/research/bee-bacteria-working-vitamin-factories |website=kaw.wallenberg.org |access-date=9 March 2022 |language=en}}</ref>
* 2017 - Extension of [[Knut and Alice Wallenberg Foundation]] of SEK 75 millions (together with [[Gunnar von Heijne]]).<ref>{{cite web | title="75 million in Wallenberg grant extension to Gunnar von Heijne - Department of Biochemistry and Biophysics" | url=https://www.dbb.su.se/about-us/news/75-million-in-wallenberg-grant-extension-to-gunnar-von-heijne-1.331289 | website=www.dbb.su.se|access-date=2021-01-14}}</ref>
